The main chemical constituents of ordinary Portland cement and their roles are:

1. **Lime ($\text{CaO}$, 60-65%):** Provides strength and soundness. Excess lime causes expansion and disintegration, while deficiency reduces strength and quickens setting.
2. **Silica ($\text{SiO}_2$, 17-25%):** Imparts strength to the cement. Excess silica prolongs the setting time.
3. **Alumina ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, 3-8%):** Responsible for quick setting. Excess alumina weakens the cement.
4. **Iron Oxide ($\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$, 0.5-6%):** Imparts color, hardness, and helps in the fusion of raw materials during manufacture.
5. **Magnesia ($\text{MgO}$, 0.5-4%):** Imparts hardness and color. Excess causes cracking and unsoundness.
6. **Calcium Sulfate / Gypsum ($\text{CaSO}_4$, 3-4%):** Added to retard or delay the initial setting time of cement.
